question.problem:
Find the center and radius of the osculating circle to the curve $r(t)$ at the point $P(1,0)$ where $t=0$, given that $‖{r}^{′}(0)‖=\sqrt{2},$ and the unit tangent vector to the curve is

$$
T(t)=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡t+\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩.
$$
question.worked_solution:
Since we are given both the value of $‖{r}^{′}(0)‖$ and the unit tangent $T(t),$ we will use the following formula for the radius of curvature:

$$
R(t)=\frac{1}{κ(t)}=\frac{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

Notice that $r(0)=⟨1,0⟩,$ since the point $P(1,0)$ is at the tip of $r(0).$ 

Now, we find ${T}^{′}(t),$ ${T}^{′}(0)$ and $‖{T}^{′}(0)‖:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t+\operatorname{cos}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩ \\ {T}^{′}(0) & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡0-\operatorname{cos}⁡0,\operatorname{cos}⁡0-\operatorname{sin}⁡0⟩=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}⟨-1,\,1⟩ \\ ‖{T}^{′}(0)‖ & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\cdot \sqrt{(-1)^{2}+{1}^{2}}=1\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the radius of curvature is

$$
\begin{aligned}R(0) & =\frac{‖{r}^{′}(0)‖}{‖{T}^{′}(0)‖}=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{1}=\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we find the principal normal vector at $t=0$ as

$$
\begin{aligned}N(0) & =\frac{{T}^{′}(0)}{‖{T}^{′}(0)‖}=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}⟨-1,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the center of the osculating circle is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(0)+R(0)N(0) & =⟨1,0⟩+\sqrt{2}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}⟨-1,1⟩=⟨0,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

The center is $(0,1)$ and the radius $\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$
